headerInfo.principles: The rules that decide every call. If a call does not serve one of these, it does not get made.
headerInfo.key: Pick the one principle you refuse to lose. Everything you call today should serve it.
headerInfo.formations: Your three fronts at a glance. Tite on early downs, Over Flex in the middle, the Mug on third and long.
headerInfo.base: Your every-down calls. The defense you live in when nothing special is on.
headerInfo.rundef: Run stopping calls. Set the edge, fill the gaps, make them one dimensional.
headerInfo.manblitz: Pressure with man behind it. Somebody comes free and everybody is covered.
headerInfo.zoneblitz: Pressure with zone behind it. Bring one, drop one, let the QB guess wrong.
headerInfo.matchcov: Match coverage. Zone eyes that turn into man the second the routes declare.
headerInfo.zonecov: Zone shells. Keep everything in front, rally and tackle, no free deep balls.
headerInfo.mancov: Man coverage. Lock them up outside and dare them to win one on one.
headerInfo.thirdLong: Their must-pass downs. Your best disguise and your best pressure.
headerInfo.redZone: Short field, no easy leverage. Make them settle for field goals.
headerInfo.constraints: Two calls that look identical pre-snap, so the picture always lies. If they solve one, the twin is dialed.

name: Alabama 3-4 Defense
subtitle: Crimson Tide · CFB 27
tagline: Control the line. Then bring everybody.

about.headline: WHAT SABAN BUILT FIRST
copy: Before the spread forced five defensive backs onto the field, Saban's Alabama lived in the 3-4. {natty|Three titles in four seasons}, 2009, 2011 and 2012, built on a nose who ate two blockers and backers who ran free.

The 2011 group gave up {ppg|8.2 points a game}, the stingiest defense of the modern era. This is that defense: control the line first, bring a nickel when you have to, and empty the cupboard on third and long.

principles.title: CONTROL THE LINE
principles.blurb: Three down, four backers. Win the line and the heavy sets die on first down.
principles.detail: The 3-4 Tite is where this defense lives. Three big bodies over the line eat the double teams, four linebackers run to the football, and the heavy sets, two tight ends, the I formation, the power run, get nothing. That is the whole idea of the early Saban defense: stop the run on early downs without ever having to cheat a safety into the box.

principles.title: THE MIDDLE GROUND
principles.blurb: 335 Over Flex brings the extra DB and keeps the size. A nickel that still stops the run.
principles.detail: When they spread you out a little, we slide to the 335 Over Flex. It brings a fifth defensive back onto the field for the nickel elements, the sim pressures and the match coverage, but we still have three down linemen and enough size to handle the run game. It is the middle of the sheet, and most of the game gets called out of it.

principles.title: OVERWHELM ON THIRD DOWN
principles.blurb: Load Dbl Mug on third and long. Two backers on the line, and the protection cannot count.
principles.detail: Get them to third and long and we go to the Load Double Mug. Two backers mugged up on the line, tackles that drop, edges that come free, six man pressure and four man sims off the exact same picture. The offensive line cannot count it, the back cannot block it, and the quarterback has to throw it early.

stats.label: RECORD 2008-2012
stats.note: Sixty one wins in five seasons, the 3-4 years.

stats.label: PTS ALLOWED / GAME
stats.note: The 2011 defense gave up eight a game. Nobody has touched it since.

stats.label: NATIONAL TITLES
stats.note: Three national championships in four seasons, 2009, 2011 and 2012.

stats.label: WIN PERCENTAGE
stats.note: Nearly ninety percent across the five 3-4 seasons.

stats.label: DEF. FIRST ROUNDERS 2010-13
stats.note: Seven first round defenders out of the 3-4: McClain, Jackson, Dareus, Barron, Kirkpatrick, Hightower, Milliner.

extras.text: Eat the double team so the man behind you runs free. Stop the run first, and the rest of the game is yours to call.

playbook.title: RUN THE VIRGINIA PLAYBOOK
playbook.note: In game, this whole defense runs out of the VIRGINIA playbook. Every front and every call on the sheet lives inside it. In Ultimate Team the same defensive playbook shows up under four other names, so any of these five gets you the exact same book.

jobs: THE NOSE OVER THE CENTER, THE ENDS ON THE TACKLES.
THREE DOWN IN TITE, THREE DOWN IN OVER FLEX.
EAT THE DOUBLE TEAMS SO FOUR BACKERS RUN FREE.
HOLD THE POINT AGAINST THE HEAVY SETS.
SLANT AND SHIFT ON EVERY SAW BLITZ.
DROP INTO THE LANES ON DT DROP.
THE TWO OUTSIDE BACKERS IN THE 3-4.
THE JACK IS THE X-FACTOR OF THIS DEFENSE.
SET THE EDGE ON FIRST DOWN, RUSH ON THIRD.
THE FREE RUNNER ON EVERY SAW BLITZ.
MUG UP ON THE LINE IN THE DOUBLE MUG.
HOVER AND RELEASE SO THE SIM COMES CLEAN.
THE TWO INSIDE BACKERS IN EVERY FRONT.
THE GREEN DOT. THEY RUN THE WHOLE SHOW.
FLOW TO THE BALL BEHIND THE THREE DOWN.
LOOP INTO THE B GAP ON THE SIMS.
FIRE DOWNHILL WHEN THE BLITZ IS CALLED.
DROP UNDER THE SEAM THROW AND TAKE IT AWAY.
THE MATCH ANCHORS OUTSIDE.
SOFT SQUAT ON THE RUN DEFENSE, FIRE DOWNHILL.
CARRY EVERY VERTICAL IN QUARTERS.
FIVE YARDS OFF, THEN ROLL UP LATE IN COVER 2 MAN.
ON AN ISLAND WHEN THE ZERO IS CALLED.
NEVER OUT OF PHASE, NEVER PANICKED.
THE BACK END THAT MAKES EVERY DISGUISE WORK.
TWO HIGH AT THE SNAP, ANYWHERE AFTER IT.
THE BACKSIDE SAFETY DROPS INTO THE BOX ON THE MACRO.
THE NICKEL COMES OUT OF THIS ROOM IN OVER FLEX.
THE BLITZING SAFETY ON EDGE BLITZ 0.
THE LAST LINE. NOTHING GETS BEHIND US.

pillars.name: 3-4 Tite
pillars.line: Three down, four backers, and the size to stop heavy sets on first down. The saw blitz brings a free rusher, the trio overload gets three on two, and the run defense macro turns Quarters into a run stopper.

checks: One of the two blitzing backers comes free whether the back blocks or not
The looper, the end and the outside backer are three on two
All eleven are in a run fit and the corners fire downhill

pillars.name: 335 Over Flex
pillars.line: The fifth defensive back comes on without giving up the size. Nickel Sim 3 gets an unblocked edge out of a four man rush, and Quarters and Palms are the coverages you live in behind it.

checks: The walked-down backer comes off the edge unblocked with only four rushing
Quarters against 2x2, Palms against trips, and the safety stays free

checks: On SS 2 Trap you are the flat first and the middle second

plays.name: Saw Blitz 0

reads.label: The Back Leaves on a Route
reads.text: If the running back releases on a route, your usered linebacker takes him in man coverage, and the pressure up the middle comes free at the quarterback.

reads.label: The Back Stays In to Block
reads.text: If the back stays in to block, one of the two blitzing linebackers still comes free. The middle of the field opens up, so read anything available over the top.

reads.label: The Quick Throw
reads.text: If the quarterback tries to dump it quickly under the pressure, your safety is sitting in position to jump the route and pick it off.

adjustments: User the non-blitzing high linebacker
Apply the zero blitz macro
Shift the D-line away from the user
Walk the user LB down one to two steps
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you need to take the game over on defense. It brings one or two rushers free almost every snap. Run it on third down, or when the offense thinks they have you figured out. The back cannot save them.

plays.name: Trio Sky Zone

reads.label: Find the Looper
reads.text: Identify the looping linebacker's side and shift the D-line away from him. That makes a three on two overload on his side: the looper, the end and the outside backer against two blockers. One of the three always comes free, and it is usually the looper.

reads.label: Seam Flats Carrying Vertical
reads.text: If the seam flats are chasing receivers vertical down the field, look straight to the back or the second player releasing to the flat. He is coming open.

reads.label: Seam Flats Sitting in the Flat
reads.text: If the seam flats drop to the flats, the middle of the field opens up. That is where the ball is going.

reads.label: The Three Receiver Hook
reads.text: Bring the three receiver down into the B gap, one to two steps opposite the looping backer. Hover, then release out to the edge to help the overload.

adjustments: Shift the D-line away from the looper
Bring the three receiver into the B gap opposite the looper
Shade the coverage: seam flats as the base, down for curls, up for hards
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want a three on two overload and a free rusher in the quarterback's face every snap. Seam flats is your base, but shade down or up to keep them guessing. Know your seam flats. If they are carrying vertical, be ready to hit the flat.

plays.name: Quarters Run Defense

reads.label: The Backside Safety
reads.text: Use the backside safety. He has fewer responsibilities, so you can be more aggressive with him. User him down into the box between the linebackers before the snap.

reads.label: Soft Squats Against the Run
reads.text: Corners in soft squats fire downhill on run plays instead of backpedaling. They are in a run fit, not a pass set, so all eleven converge on the football.

reads.label: Soft Squats Against a Vertical
reads.text: If the number one receiver goes vertical, the soft squat corner matches him up the field, so you are not fully exposed deep despite the aggressive look.

reads.label: The Flat Is the Hole
reads.text: If a route attacks the flat quickly, the soft squat corner can jump it and give up the vertical behind him. This is built for run spammers, not balanced offenses.

adjustments: Apply the run defense macro
User the backside safety into the box
Set the corners to soft squats
plays.whenToUse: Call this when your opponent is running it eight out of ten plays. This is your run stopper: aggressive D-line, backers flying downhill, a safety in the box, corners in run fits. If they are balanced, go back to normal Quarters. This is for run spammers.

plays.name: Nickel Sim 3

reads.label: The Unblocked Edge
reads.text: The walked-down linebacker blitzes off the edge while the backside linebacker loops into the B gap opposite him. That is unblocked pressure out of a four man rush.

reads.label: Count the Blockers
reads.text: If the offense keeps extra blockers in for the sim, you have won the numbers. Six blocking four means fewer routes for seven defenders to cover.

reads.label: The Shell Stays Whole
reads.text: Only four are rushing, so the back end stays full. Curl flats to protect over the top, hard flats to take away the easy completion, depending on down and distance.

reads.label: If It Gets Picked Up
reads.text: Even if the pressure gets absorbed, you gave up nothing in coverage. Still four rushing, still seven back, still able to contest every vertical.

adjustments: Shade the flats: curl flats or hard flats
Bring the backside LB into the B gap opposite the blitz
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you want unblocked heat without selling out the coverage. Third and long, fourth and long, any pass-heavy situation where you need a turnover. A four man rush with a free hitter is as good as it gets.

plays.name: Quarters and Palms

reads.label: Trips: Call Palms
reads.text: Against trips, call Palms. You get match coverage across the board with the safety free in the middle of the field.

reads.label: 2x2: Call Quarters
reads.text: Against 2x2 sets, call Quarters. Every receiver gets boxed and the windows close.

reads.label: Bunch and Flood
reads.text: Against bunch or flood, Palms keeps the safety free in the middle and takes away the shot over the top.

reads.label: It Plays the Run
reads.text: Both coverages let the defenders fly down and make plays against the run while you still rush four up front.

plays.whenToUse: These are your baseline coverages. Run them every game and mix them with your blitzes and other looks so they never know you are just running match. Quarters when they are 2x2, Palms when they go trips. Box everything and let the front get pressure.

plays.name: Red Zone DT Drop

reads.label: Your Assignment
reads.text: User the linebacker on the backside, opposite the two dropping tackles. Keep him on the outside edge so the pressure comes unblocked.

reads.label: They Send Everybody Out
reads.text: If the offense releases every eligible receiver, the edge comes in completely unblocked and blows up the quarterback. That is the best case.

reads.label: They Keep Blockers In
reads.text: If they keep extra blockers in to pick up the edge, the two tackles drop into the hook and curl zones and sit in the passing lanes over the middle.

reads.label: Tackles in Coverage
reads.text: Dropped tackles create double coverage in the middle of the field. Even with time, there is nowhere to throw it inside.

adjustments: User the backside linebacker, away from the dropping tackles
plays.whenToUse: Call this in the red zone when you need a disguised pressure that punishes them no matter what they do. They block up, your tackles are sitting in the lanes. They release everybody, your edge comes untouched. There is no good answer.

plays.name: LB Blitz 6

reads.label: The Free Edge
reads.text: If the offense does not account for the walked-down outside linebacker, you get a free rusher off the edge. Let it cook.

reads.label: The Back Blocks
reads.text: If they keep the back in to block, they are releasing fewer routes. Play over the middle as the user and find the first receiver coming free.

reads.label: Patrol the Middle
reads.text: You are the outside backer opposite the two-deep tackles. Hover over the middle and pick up whatever comes open. You are covering the vert hook and the three receiver zones at once.

reads.label: Match on the Back End
reads.text: The secondary is playing Cover 6 match behind it. Trust the DBs on their assignments. Your only job is the middle and whatever leaks through.

adjustments: Shift the D-line away from the linebackers
Slant the D-line out
Blitz all the linebackers
User the backer opposite the two-deep tackles
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you need heat and coverage at the same time. A free rusher with match coverage behind it. Either they get pressured into a bad throw or they block the blitz and hand you the middle of the field. You win both ways.

plays.name: SS 2 Trap

reads.label: The Setup Is the Macro
reads.text: It runs off the zone blitz macro. Find it under the macros on Scheme Kings, set it up, then press L1 for the zone blitz. That is the whole setup.

reads.label: Your Player
reads.text: User the outside linebacker on the line opposite the blitz. Hover, then get out. The free rusher comes off the blitz side.

reads.label: Nobody in the Flat
reads.text: There is no flat defender on your side, so you are the flat. Get out to it first. If nothing shows in the flat, peel back over the middle and pick up whatever you see.

reads.label: Something in the Flat
reads.text: If they send everybody out and a route shows in the flat, take it away right now. That is the quick throw he wants under the pressure.

reads.label: The Rest Is Covered
reads.text: Both vert hooks match the verticals up the field and the safeties are over the top. With the rusher unblocked, he has to throw it early into all of that.

adjustments: Apply the zone blitz macro, then L1 zone blitz
User the outside linebacker on the line, opposite the blitz
plays.whenToUse: A base 3-4 call for heavier personnel, but it holds up against anything. Set the macro, user the backside backer, play the flat first and the middle second, and let the free rusher off the blitz side do the rest.

plays.name: Saw Blitz 1

reads.label: Read the Nose
reads.text: Before the snap, find which way the nose tackle is slanting. That decides which way you shift the D-line.

reads.label: The Free Edge
reads.text: After you shift and slant the line to the nose's side, the edge opposite the shift produces a free rusher. Look for the gap left by the backer hovering away from the shift.

reads.label: Routes Versus Blockers
reads.text: If they send everybody on routes, the blitzing edge comes free almost every time. If they keep extra blockers in, the pressure can get picked up, so lean on the safety help over the top.

reads.label: Man With Help
reads.text: User the middle linebacker in man and hover him in the hole away from the shift. The safety over the top means there are no one on one shots downfield even when the blitz is blocked.

adjustments: Shift the D-line to the nose's slant side
Slant the D-line out after the shift
Put the edge on QB contain
User the MLB away from the shift
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you need a guaranteed pressure package. Find the nose's slant, shift and slant the line out, contain the quarterback, and bring your backer down on the opposite side. They send routes, you get a free rusher. Simple as that.

plays.name: Cover 4 Quarters

reads.label: 2x2
reads.text: Play Quarters straight up. The user takes any vertical or crossing threat, and the match keeps you step for step on deep posts and seams.

reads.label: 3x1 and Trips
reads.text: Quarters is not as strong here as Palms, but it holds out of the 3-4. Know your responsibilities and stay disciplined on the zone matchups.

reads.label: Bunch
reads.text: Quarters plays well against bunch. If they motion out to 2x2, adjust with the safety and stay in your Quarters rules.

reads.label: Run Fits
reads.text: Everybody flows to the football. Quarters keeps the run fits intact, so the safeties and the backers fly downhill against heavy formations.

adjustments: vs motion to 2x2, user the safety across
vs a run-heavy team, apply the run defense macro
plays.whenToUse: Call this when you do not know if they are running or passing and you do not want to bring pressure. I form, single back with multiple tight ends, big formations. This is your base call. It stops the run and adapts to any passing scheme. When you are not in your blitz packages, this is where you live.

plays.name: Edge Blitz 0

reads.label: The Back Blocks
reads.text: When the back stays in to block, you have unblocked pressure coming free. Move the usered linebacker over the middle to take away the quick throw.

reads.label: The Back Routes Out
reads.text: When the back leaves on a route, he goes into man coverage. The pressure comes off the edge and through the loop, and more than one rusher can come free.

reads.label: Looper or Edge
reads.text: Read which rusher comes free. Sometimes it is the looper from the second level, sometimes the edge. The blitzing safety comes free almost every time.

adjustments: User the linebacker opposite the blitz
Bring the linebacker down one to two steps
QB contain if he is a runner
plays.whenToUse: Run this when you need to get after the quarterback and force a quick, bad decision. It is a zero blitz, so everybody is in man. If the back leaks out you have him covered and you still get heat. Mix it in against shotgun runs too, because your guys are flying downhill.

plays.name: Cover 2 Man

reads.label: The Depth Disguise
reads.text: Start the safeties at nine and the corners at five to mirror your Quarters look. Roll everybody up right before the snap so the press does not show early.

reads.label: Inside Shade on the Slot
reads.text: With safety help over the top, play a heavy inside shade on the slot to take away the inside breaking route. Make him try to beat you deep, where the safety is waiting.

reads.label: The Back Out of the Backfield
reads.text: Get underneath the back's route in the flat. Even if he looks like he has a step, the safety over the top closes and separates him from the ball.

reads.label: Two Over the Top
reads.text: With two safeties deep, any vertical that looks open is covered. Trust the shell. Quarterbacks throw into it thinking the receiver is open over the top.

adjustments: Safeties at nine, corners at five, then roll up late
Press the corners late (L2, left stick down)
Heavy inside shade on the slot
plays.whenToUse: Call this when they think they have figured out your Quarters. You are still giving them the two high shell, but now you are in man underneath. Mix it with your blitzes and with Cover 4 and they never know what is coming. This is the change-up that wins games.

plays.name: Red Zone DT Drop 0

reads.label: The Back Releases
reads.text: If the back leaves on a route, both edge rushers come in completely unblocked. The quarterback barely gets to the top of his drop.

reads.label: The Back Blocks
reads.text: Even when the back stays in to block, you still get at least one unblocked rusher. The blitz works either way.

reads.label: Your Coverage
reads.text: User the outside linebacker away from the blitz side. It is man everywhere else, so take away anything quick and easy underneath.

reads.label: The Escape Hatch
reads.text: If he feels the pressure and dumps it to the back, you are step for step in man. Wipe it out. If he holds it, he goes down or forces a throw you can pick off.

adjustments: User the outside linebacker away from the blitz
Slant the D-line toward the walked-down backers
plays.whenToUse: Call this in the red zone when you need a stop. It does not matter if they keep the back in or send him out, you are getting pressure either way. Man everywhere else, take away the quick game, and let the two free rushers do the work. Flip the stick twice and watch it fire.

plays.name: Nickel Sim 2

reads.label: The Back Blocks
reads.text: If the back stays in and they block with five, you are still only rushing four. You win in coverage, seven defenders on four routes. Sit back, everything is bagged, take the sack.

reads.label: The Back Leaks Out
reads.text: If the back releases, the line cannot account for all the rushers. Expect one or two edge rushers coming free. Get home fast.

reads.label: The Seam Throw
reads.text: When the quarterback feels the edge collapsing he tries to fit it into the seam. Your dropping backer steps underneath that throw. The pick is there.

reads.label: Hover, Then Release
reads.text: As the user on the outside backer on the line, hover to hold the blockers' eyes, then release. Do not engage. Engaging frees a blocker onto the wrong man. Get out and let the sim rusher come clean.

adjustments: Shade the coverage at the setup
User the outside backer on the line: hover, then release
plays.whenToUse: Call this on third and medium to long when you want free pressure without selling out the coverage. You are only rushing four, so even if they pick it up you still outnumber the routes. A no-lose call: you get the sack or you suffocate every route.

home.pitch: Three down and four backers on early downs, slide to Over Flex in the middle, bury them in the Mug on third and long.

book.note: every front and every call on the sheet lives inside it
